cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

At least 1 year demonstrated experience with troubleshooting, maintenance, and advanced use of one or more of the following equipment types: DSLR cameras, Audio mics/recorders, 3D printers, or Laser cutters.
Library experience, including knowledge of circulation practices, policy, and software management tools such as Springshare and Alma.
Experience leading the work of others including a demonstrated ability to monitor and direct the work of others.
Experience supervising, training, and developing student employees.
Demonstrated experience working in a collaborative, team-based work environment.

At least 1 year experience in a makerspace environment (such as community, academic, or personal) working with technical equipment (e.g. a laser cutter, 3D printer, or computer aided cutting machine).
Demonstrated experience working with the public in a service-oriented environment.
Under the direction of the Director of the University Library Center for Digital Scholarship, the Digital Scholarship Associate is responsible for:
Maintain Library Management System records for Digital Scholarship equipment and keep up with best practices.
Provide supervision to approximately 20 casual employees (student assistants) in both the David Kirk Digital Scholarship Commons and the Digital Scholarship Innovation Studio.

Serve as the Digital Scholarship lead on equipment checkout policy and collections best practices and implementation. Frequently collaborate with other library departments in support of equipment checkout such as Metadata Services and User Services & Resource Sharing.
Assist patrons in-person at multiple service desks and virtually through email and live chat.
Administer the Digital Scholarship billing/overdue and fine policies. Respond to Digital Scholarship billing appeals. Exercises independent judgment in waiving fines.
Participate in Digital Scholarship department meetings.
Directing and monitoring the daily operations at the Digital Scholarship Commons Service Desk (DSC) at McHenry Library

Work with Digital Scholarship librarians to manage the organization and ordering of equipment for the DSC and the DSI through CruzBuy and OneCard systems, including new equipment, replacement parts, pieces for equipment kits, and other operational needs.
Support the development of student employees with varying levels of prior work and technical experience.

Provide input on strategic directions and goals related to Digital Scholarship policy, collections, and circulation, working with the Director of the Library Center for Digital Scholarship and other library departments as required to identify and lead related initiatives.
Manage and resolve difficult patron interactions.
Act as Digital Scholarship liaison to User Services & Resource Sharing team and Alma/Primo team
Seek out and participate in recommended professional development opportunities.
Directing and monitoring the daily operations at the Digital Scholarship Innovation Studio (DSI)
Supervise the work of the Digital Scholarship Student Leads to maintain equipment and equipment records.
Manage student hiring process: Write job descriptions, recruitment justifications, post staff vacancies for recruitment, make hiring decisions or recommend student workers to be hired.

Direct and monitor the daily operations of the Digital Scholarship Commons Service Desk at McHenry Library and the Digital Scholarship Innovation Studio Service Desk at the Science & Engineering Library.
Assist in triage of Digital Scholarship email tickets
Support the Director of the Library Center for Digital Scholarship with short- and long-term planning for the department.
Participate in unit, department, library, and systemwide initiatives. Assist other units as necessary and participate in ad-hoc special projects as assigned.
at the Science & Engineering Library

Oversee safe equipment use, safety procedures/training, and working with the library operations team and campus Environmental Health and Safety to ensure equipment and environment meet campus standards.
Train Digital Scholarship student workers on Alma, Springshare, and other software systems

Inform patrons of library policies related to Digital Scholarship materials; teach patrons how to locate materials and how to look up digital scholarship equipment related materials; refer requests as appropriate.

Check materials in and out, place holds, recalls, and searches; renew materials; assign barcodes to materials that have never been checked out; answer phones, transfer calls and take messages; accept materials for digital scholarship equipment related processing.
Support Digital Scholarship events, including event planning, setup/takedown of materials, and incorporating student help as appropriate.
Managing and supervising students that work for the Library Center for Digital Scholarship
Troubleshoot and perform repairs to equipment, including researching potential solutions, communicating with vendors, and consulting with digital scholarship librarians as needed.
Collaborate with Digital Scholarship Librarians to identify, schedule, and support training opportunities for Digital Scholarship related equipment for student workers.

Provide patron education and support for Digital Scholarship supported technology in the DSC and the DSI, such as audio equipment in the Audio Production Studio, video equipment in the Video Production Studio, and makerspace equipment in the Digital Scholarship Innovation Studio.
Maintain confidentiality as required by Library, University, and system-wide policy.
Developing and implementing policies and procedures for use of library circulation systems
Maintain, update, and perform regular equipment inventory.
Maintain a student manual for student worker related work in collaboration with Digital Scholarship staff and librarians.
Assist patrons in identifying the appropriate Digital Scholarship equipment for their needs and direct unresolved issues as appropriate.
Execute emergency procedures as outlined in the Library Emergency Manual.
Developing and implementing policies and procedures for the DSC & DSI
Assist with implementation of new technology as needed.

Work with the Digital Scholarship team to maintain consistent student worker policies across both spaces, including performance expectations, monitoring performance, providing corrective action, and recommending employee selection, corrective action, and dismissals.
Managing and maintaining equipment in both the DSC & DSI
Serve as the Digital Scholarship point of contact for Library ITS in relation to DSC and DSI space needs, including lab software updates and lab and media viewing rooms equipment repairs.

Ensure that student schedules for the DSC and DSI provide adequate coverage for library users. Coordinate student backup where available. When student coverage is not sufficient to meet desk coverage needs, work on the affected desk or coordinate desk closure as a last resort.
Participating in library-wide and system-wide committees
Maintain and update website content related to equipment and spaces.
Participating in section-wide cross-training and process improvement activities
Demonstrated ability to take initiative and learn new technology and equipment to effectively support operations.

Written and oral communication skills with sufficient ability to explain complex, technical concepts to users from a variety of technical backgrounds using various communication methods (e.g. in person or online, synchronous or asynchronous).
Interpersonal skills sufficient to work collaboratively with library staff, student assistants, and users with diverse backgrounds including providing leadership to other library staff members
Demonstrated ability to give, receive, evaluate, and apply constructive feedback.
Demonstrated ability to adapt to changing work dynamics such as setting priorities with competing deadlines
Analytical skills sufficient to interpret numerical data to form reasonable conclusions.
Demonstrated ability working with multiple software systems for the purpose of connecting workflows, tracking materials, and communicating.
